member.name: _scanFloorSeconds
member.para: What the lowering cost where it bought nothing. Measured on "Die Cyber-Brutzellen" (builds 331 and 339, 2026-08-17). Chapter 14 is recovered inside a gap re-probe at a genuine 1.01 s break - 0.7575 s once scaled, hence clamped to the floor - which floored the threshold at minute 11 of the run with chapters 16-29, about 9.5 hours of audio, still to scan: 921 -> 2177 probes, 26.5 -> 55.7 minutes, Whisper audio 4:20:51 -> 12:13:36. It bought nothing. Build 331 is the control experiment, its Probe having run at 2.5 s throughout because the identical lowering landed in Re-probe when nothing was left to scan: all 29 chapters at identical positions, and the seven that build 339 accepted "at a silence" (16, 18, 20, 21, 23, 27, 29) were accepted "at a jingle" by build 331 at the same millisecond. That book's chapters are announced after music; the extra silence candidates only won the race to the same announcement.

Where the lowering does pay, and through which consumer. "I Shall Wear Midnight" chapter 9 sits behind a 0.74 s break where the book's other thirteen run 4.47-5.25 s, and it was recovered by the sub-floor sweep, not by the scan gate; "Paula Monti" chapters 4 and 12 likewise. No corpus mark is known to depend on the forward scan's own gate having come down. A book whose breaks really are short still throttles itself through its own forward scan: "De vandrande djäknarne" reaches 0.8 s from chapter 3, a primary-scan mark.

member.name: JingleCandidate
member.para: How wide the old blip-driven windows got. A candidate that started at the jingle's first note and ran past the announcement was bounded by nothing but the music's own length: 9 of the corpus's 20 marks found that way came from windows of 33 s or more, four of them 51-60 s - well past the width exists to warn about.

The corpus split that sets the order of the two looks. 225 marks sit after the music against 20 inside it, so reading the speech behind the music first means the second look at the music itself is rarely paid for at all.

member.name: ExtendToPlannedSeam
member.para: What reading ahead saved over a whole book. Measured on BARDIOC.m4b's 15.6 h debug log (2026-08-01, 1659 probe decodes): 1814 encoder passes without reading ahead, 1570 with it, 244 windows served from cache that had cost a pass each - and not one decode made longer than the passes it already bought.

What stopping at the chunk boundary would have saved instead. A further 124 passes - and it was refused anyway, because every planned end is snapped to a silence or non-speech mid-point while a chunk boundary is not, so the cache would end mid-speech and an announcement straddling the cut would be lost on both sides of it.

member.name: RereadDenoisedAsync
member.para: The transcript that lost a chapter. On "De vandrande djäknarne" chapter 1 the recognizer wrote "1. Jäknuktåg" - the number and the chapter's title, with "Första kapitlet" collapsed into the digit - so no wording of the phrase could match and the chapter was lost.

What denoising recovers, measured. Across 22 window framings 20 ms apart over that announcement, ggml-small recovers the chapter word from 10 of them on the raw audio and from all 22 denoised, at a steady p≈0.6 instead of a notation that swung between "1. Kapitlet – Gjäknupptåg", "1. KAPITLET", "1. KAPITLÄT", "1. KJÄKNUGTÅG" and "1. Jäknuktåg". It is also cheaper than the alternative that works equally well: medium and large-v3-turbo read it at every framing too, at 2-3x the decode cost of a denoise plus a re-read.

member.name: RereadInOnePassAsync
member.para: The decode grid behind the re-read width. Gruelfin.m4b's prologue was lost first to a 50 s window (2026-07-30) and again to build 280's classified one (2026-08-09), which is exactly wide. Re-measured on the live decode at 0:03:20.19 with ggml-small, "Prolog." is read at 22.0, 23.5 and 25.0 s and gone at 27.0 and 30.0 s - identically on both of this project's machines, which is rare enough to be worth stating.

What a narrower planned window would have cost. 2 of the fourteen-book corpus's 220 jingle marks are accepted 26.2 s and 28.3 s into their window ("Die Dritte Macht" 8:06:31, "Die Maahks" 10:11:27, 2026-08-09), so narrowing at planning time would have traded this prologue for them.

member.name: CacheHidesTheExpectation
member.para: The run-on that lost a chapter with no pass ever reading it. "The Forever War" chapter 1 (2026-08-08), and the shape is not exotic. The candidate at 0:01:14.36 was handed 23.2 s spanning two announcements - the publisher's title card, a 5 s pause, then "Chapter 1" - and Whisper returned the whole window as one run-on segment reading "And now, the FOREVER WAR." (p=0.62), the announcement simply absent from it. That is ordinary recognizer behaviour on a long window and not something this pass can prevent. What it can prevent is the second half: the chapter's own candidate at 0:01:21.66 - whose window opens 3 s before the announcement and reads "CHAPTER 1" cleanly when decoded (verified with the wprobe harness) - was served that run-on from the cache, and the segment starting 7 s before its window was then dropped as out of range. The chapter was lost with no pass ever having read it, and, being chapter 1, no sequence gap to notice.

member.name: CacheableEnd
member.para: The announcement lost for a whole run to a decode the recognizer stopped short of. "BARDIOC.m4b" (2026-08-02): the "Zeittafel" announcement at 0:00:51. The probe at 0:00:00 planned a window to 0:00:40.73 and read ahead to 0:00:54.19; handed 54 s beginning with ~20 s of jingle music, Whisper stopped emitting at 0:00:37. The unread 17 s went into the cache as if empty, the next two candidates (a VAD jingle region at 0:00:19.48, a silence end at 0:00:43.33) were both served from it, and the next fresh decode began at 0:00:54.19 - past the phrase. Replayed through the real decoder and recognizer, the tail decode this rule restores (0:00:40.73-0:01:10.69) reads "Zeittafel 1971 bis 1984..." at p=0.72, and so do windows framed from 0:00:43.33 and 0:00:46. Nothing else could have caught it: Silero hears no speech at all between 0:00:23.3 and 0:00:54.56 at any threshold from 0.50 to 0.70, so the announcement is not a blip could have found either.

member.name: ProbeContext.SecondGuessNumbers
member.para: The mishearing that refuted "a wider window is already the remedy". "Die Cyber-Brutzellen" (2026-08-01): an announcement 27 s deep into a 44 s window came back as chapter 40 instead of 14. The wider window is what produced the mishearing, so Probe's own sequence-gap re-probe is no longer exempted from questioning its numbers.

member.name: _subFloorSeconds
member.para: The worked example. "Paula Monti": its threshold came down to 0.8 s, its chapter breaks measure 1.39-1.49 s, and not one of them was ever a candidate - its five gaps each re-probed one or two candidates to no effect and were all closed later by a sub-floor sweep.

member.name: _gapAbove
member.para: The announcement accepted unquestioned. On "Die Cyber-Brutzellen" (2026-08-01) an announcement read as chapter 40 was accepted inside a gap re-probe while held a missing set containing exactly one number.

member.name: FindUnheardJingleSpeech
member.para: The stretched segment timestamp that vetoed a re-read. Observed on a BARDIOC.m4b clip around chapter 21 (2026-07-30), where a 56 s window lost "Kapitel 21" exactly as Gruelfin's did while a 25 s one read it cleanly - but a segment reading "können." claimed 41.08-54.76 and so covered the jingle it had no words for.

member.name: RecoverUnnumberedAnnouncementsAsync
member.para: The chapter that read differently from two window widths. Chapter 13 of "I Shall Wear Midnight" was read as "CHAPTER XIII" from the 16.1 s window it was probed with and as "Chapter 13" from a 48.8 s one over the same announcement (2026-07-30).

member.name: AcceptNamedMatchAsync
member.para: The mid-book false match that displaced a real epilogue. "Corsa nello spazio" (2026-08-05), where /epilogo/ matching inside "riepilogo" at 13:35:19 displaced the genuine epilogue found at 18:18:57 - which is why "later" is measured in the file rather than in the order the passes happened to hear things.

member.name: ReprobeGapCandidatesAsync
member.para: The duplicate marks that made stopping worth doing. Confirmed on BARDIOC.m4b 2026-07-30, where the chapter 10 that closed the gap was re-found and re-refined by the three following candidates - four identical marks at 5:14:48.15, about two minutes of pure waste.

member.name: GatherLongestPauseFirstAsync
member.para: 0.75 is where the descent stops paying, measured rather than inherited (2026-08-19, replayed over the frozen build-341 logs). Total probes for the whole shape, first half plus second, at four values of the tighten factor - Forever War 260 / 448 / 769 / 769 at 0.75 / 0.60 / 0.50 / 0.40; I Shall Wear Midnight 118 / 161 / 222 / 373; Rendezvous With Rama 82 / 146 / 172 / 263; The Philosopher's Stone 94 / 94 / 95 / 97. Loosening it recovers Forever War's chapters 6 and 7 inside the first half at a cost of 188 probes, and the second half recovers them anyway. So the constant the file-order gate already uses is also the right one here, and there is no second knob to add.

Stopping on a reading rather than on a placed mark costs nothing (same replay). Simulating both signals over the seven books whose logs carry enough transcripts gives identical stop ranks: Corsa 71, De vandrande djaeknarne 82, I Shall Wear Midnight 33, Rama 46, Forever War 77, The Philosopher's Stone 14, Wintersmith 54. The candidates that hold a reading without becoming a chapter all rank below where the walk stops - Forever War's deepest such candidate is rank 589, against a stop at 77. Two honest limits on that: the reading detector in the replay was a regex approximation of , not the real matcher, and the logs only carry transcripts for candidates the build-341 walk actually probed, which over the top ranks is 74 % to 100 % per book except Forever War at 39 %. The stop ranks are therefore a lower bound.

The pause-length distribution carries no knee, so the floor could not be derived from it (rejected 2026-08-19, measured first). The stored candidate list is already truncated at --min-silence-length, so its median sits just above that floor and the spread above it is narrow: Corsa's entire candidate range is 2.13 s (median) to 4.03 s (longest) across an 18-hour book holding 65 chapters. A "stop below N times the median" rule stops Corsa at rank 0, Wintersmith at 5 and Paula Monti at 1, and De vandrande djaeknarne's deepest chapter anchor is below its own median. Chapter breaks are not outliers in the stored set; the stored floor already cut the distribution where the interesting part begins.

member.name: DryStartBudget
member.para: Verified probe for probe on the one book that exercises it (2026-08-19). Mort is the corpus's early-abort case - a book with no chapter announcements at all - and its candidate list predicts 83 candidates inside the default 60-minute --early-abort window. Its build-341 log gives up after exactly 83 probes: with nothing found, no threshold is ever learned, so the file-order walk skips nothing and reads precisely that set. The budget is therefore not an analogy to --early-abort, it is the same spend.

It never bites a book the shape can help. Seven of the eight pause-announced corpus books find their first chapter anchor at rank 1 to 6, far inside budgets of 4 to 78. The one book it does cut is De vandrande djaeknarne, whose first anchor sits at rank 35 against a budget of 17 - and that costs 17 probes and a handover to the file-order walk, which is the shape that book would have had anyway.

member.name: GatherThenResolveAsync
member.para: The two-half shape was built first, and a clip proved it loses a part restart (2026-08-19, build 359, "fw-restart" - a 53-minute clip of The Forever War, whose numbering restarts). Read as a descending half followed by a pause half over the unsettled stretches, the way the jingle-first shape is: the descent read 2 of 80 candidates, found part 2's chapter 1 at 0:25:14, and the head stretch behind it was then bounded above by chapter 1 - so part 1's chapter 15 at 0:03:03 was heard and refused with "skipped chapter 15 - at or above 1, this gap's upper bound". Lifting that bound made it heard and accepted, and it was then dropped anyway by the sequence repair ("contradicts its neighbours"), because a restart is recognized by watching the numbering fall and climb again and no walk confined to one stretch can watch that. The one-sweep control run over the same clip on the same binary writes 5 chapters in 2 parts (15, 1-4); the two-half descending run writes 4.

Reading the descent as a plan rather than as a first half fixes it outright, and costs nothing: the saving was never in deferring the conclusions, only in not reading the windows, and one forward walk still reads no more windows than the two halves did.

member.name: ProposeThreshold
member.para: What the running minimum actually prunes (replayed over all seventeen frozen build-366 logs, 2026-08-20; scratchpad\anchor_dist.py, reading the gate in force from each log's own "threshold tightened/lowered" lines rather than reconstructing it, so a recovery mark that build 341 withholds from the scan gate cannot skew the figure). Corpus-wide it skips 3075 of 11236 candidates, and almost all of that is five books: Die Cyber-Brutzellen 1852, The Forever War 649, Wintersmith 256, The Philosopher's Stone 209, Corsa 109.

On the other nine it prunes nothing at all, and the cause is not this method. Those books place every mark at a jingle - BARDIOC 25, Raumschiff Erde 39, Die Dritte Macht 35, Gruelfin 33, Das Mutantenkorps 30, Stalker 29, Die Maahks 26 - and a jingle mark is deliberately never handed here (see ), because the hush around music says nothing about how long the book's chapter breaks are. So the gate never leaves its --min-silence-length starting value and skips 0 of 6524 candidates on them. This corrects a long-standing suspicion that the running minimum was being pinned low by one tight transition on such a book: on Die Dritte Macht the 0.54 s silence that was blamed for it is irrelevant, since no threshold is ever proposed there at all.

Relaxing the minimum to a 10th percentile was measured and is not worth it. Over the same logs it would skip 3815 rather than 3075, and every bit of the difference is two books - I Shall Wear Midnight 0 -> 310 and Rendezvous With Rama 0 -> 468, both sitting at the 0.8 s floor today because one genuinely short break pinned them. On The Forever War it would skip fewer (649 -> 610), and on the other five it changes nothing, their anchor spreads being far too tight for a percentile to differ from the minimum (Corsa min 3.04 / p10 3.07, Rama 4.04 / 4.07, Wintersmith 2.98 / 3.00). About fifteen minutes across seventeen books, against a change that moves which windows Probe opens.

Two other relaxations, rejected on soundness rather than on cost. Pruning by a raw percentile of the file's own silence distribution would have worked on Stalker only by luck: that book's Zeittafel anchor is the 5.49 s silence, rank 1 of 5962, so any percentile cut keeps it - but had it been rank ~400 (~2.0 s) a p95 cut at 2.96 s would have skipped it and lost the mark permanently, with nothing in the output to say so. And tightening from rejected probes is worse than useless: a probe that finds nothing at a long silence carries no positive information about how long a chapter's silence is, and if it argues for anything it argues for lowering the threshold.

Distribution figures for the two books those rejections were reasoned on, since they are not cheap to recover: Stalker has 5962 silences of at least 1.0 s, 1032 of at least 1.5 s and 158 of at least 2.0 s (median 1.22 s, p90 1.61, p95 1.75, max 5.49); Die Dritte Macht 727 candidates against 759 probes.
